source_text: Πᾶς δὲ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου δεχθήτω: ἔπειτα δὲ δοκιμάσαντες αὐτὸν γνώσεσθε, σύνεσιν γὰρ ἕξετε δεξιὰν καὶ ἀριστεράν. εἰ μὲν παρόδιός ἐστιν ὁ ἐρχόμενος, βοηθεῖτε αὐτῷ, ὅσον δύνασθε: οὐ μενεῖ δὲ πρὸς ὑμᾶς εἰ μὴ δύο ἡ τρεῖς ἡμέρας, ἑὰν ᾖ ἀνάγκη. εἰ δὲ θέλει πρὸς ὑμᾶς καθῆσθαι, τεχνίτης ὤν, ἐργαζέσθω καὶ φαγέτω. εἰ δὲ οὐκ ἔχει τέχνην, κατὰ τὴν σύνεσιν ὑμῶν προνοήσατε, πῶς μὴ ἀργὸς μεθ̓ ὑμῶν ζήσεται Χριστιανός. εἰ δ’ οὐ θέλει οὕτω ποιεῖν, χριστέμπορός ἐστι: προσέχετε ἀπὸ τῶν τοιούτων.
pass_a_gloss: But whoever comes in name of Lord let him be received; then having tested him you will know, for you will have right and left understanding. If the one coming is a traveler, assist him as much as you are able: he will not stay with you except two or three days, unless there is necessity. If he wants to stay with you, being a craftsman, let him work and eat. If he does not have a craft, provide for him according to your understanding, how a Christian will not live idly with you. If he does not want to do thus, he is a Christ-trafficker: beware of such ones.

choices.why: literal translation of the compound word

choices.term: πῶς μὴ ἀργὸς μεθ̓ ὑμῶν ζήσεται
choices.english: how a Christian will not live idly with you
choices.why: preserving the negative and the preposition
rejected: so that he will not live idly among you

pass_b_english: Welcome everyone who comes in the name of the Lord. After you have tested them, you will know them, because you will have discernment on both sides. If the person who comes is just passing through, help them as much as you can; they will not stay with you more than two or three days, unless there is a pressing need. If they want to settle with you and they have a trade, let them work and eat. If they have no trade, use your own judgment to provide for them, so that a Christian will not live idly among you. If they refuse to do this, they are a trafficker in Christ; watch out for such people.

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: All clauses in the Greek source [p1] are accounted for in both Pass A and Pass B. Pass A is a faithful literal translation, and Pass B is a faithful fluent rendering. The distinction between 'with you' (μεθ̓ ὑμῶν) and 'among you' is a minor stylistic variation. The translation of 'χριστέμπορός' as 'Christ-trafficker' is accurate to the Greek compound.
